description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Somaliland Programme works to unlock the trade potential of one of the Horn of Africa's most strategically positioned but underserved territories, operating since 2020 in partnership with the Government of Somaliland and the private sector along the Berbera Corridor, a route of growing regional significance connecting landlocked Ethiopia to the Port of Berbera. The Programme advances trade facilitation across five interconnected areas: strengthening the trade and investment environment through policy and regulatory reform aligned with regional frameworks; improving the quality and value of traded goods through standards and sanitary and phytosanitary capacity building in support of key export sectors including livestock, which dominates Somaliland's trade; advancing digital trade systems to modernise customs processes and reduce transaction costs; improving physical connectivity at key border and port infrastructure nodes; and promoting greener, more resilient, and inclusive trade with a deliberate focus on women traders and small-scale cross-border participants who have historically been excluded from formal trade channels.
Hargeisa is the capital city of Somalia

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.
